chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said:

I heard Ibn Abi Layla narrating to his companions, saying: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) judged between two men who had traveled together. When they intended to have breakfast, one of them took out five loaves of bread from his provisions, and the other took out three loaves. A passerby passed by them, so they invited him to their food. The man ate with them until nothing remained. When they had finished, the passerby gave them eight dirhams as payment for what he had eaten from their food.

Then the owner of the three loaves said to the owner of the five loaves, 'Divide them into two halves between me and you.' But the owner of the five loaves said, 'No, each of us should take from the dirhams according to the number of loaves he brought from the provisions.'
So they went to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) regarding that matter. When he heard their statement, he said to them, 'Reach an agreement, for your case is trivial.'
They said, 'Judge between us with the truth.' He said, 'So he gave the owner of the five loaves seven dirhams, and he gave the owner of the three loaves one dirham.'
And he said to them, 'Did not one of you take out five loaves from his provisions, and the other take out three?' They said, 'Yes.'
He said, 'Did not your guest eat with you the same amount that you ate?' They said, 'Yes.'
He said, 'Did not each of you eat three loaves and a third?' They said, 'Yes.'
He said, 'Did you not, O owner of the three, eat three loaves and a third, and did you not, O owner of the five, eat three loaves and a third, and did the guest not eat three loaves and a third?'
'Is it not that there remained for you, O owner of the three, one-third of a loaf from your provisions, and there remained for you, O owner of the five, two loaves and a third?'

And you ate three loaves and a third. So he gave them to each one-third of a loaf, one dirham. So he gave the owner of the two loaves and a third seven dirhams, and he gave the owner of the one-third of a loaf one dirham.'
ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali distribute the payment between two travelers who shared their bread with a guest?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, illustrates Imam Ali’s (AS) application of proportional equity (nisab) in commercial disputes, moving beyond simple arithmetic to account for the guest's share of each loaf. It is a cornerstone in Shia jurisprudence for establishing that contributions are measured by actual consumption rather than mere possession, a principle often cited in discussions of fair trade and inheritance. The narrative highlights the Imam’s methodical questioning to ensure both parties understood the logical basis of the ruling, reinforcing the importance of justice (adl) in social transactions.
